item.title: Fiji FA CEO backs World Cup dream
item.description: FOR generations, Fiji football fans have dreamt of seeing the national team compete on football’s biggest stage, the FIFA World Cup, and that ambition could become a reality within the next decade. Fiji Football Association CEO Mohammed Yusuf says achieving World Cup qualification will require patience, planning and continued investment as the country competes against 211 FIFA member associations
item.content:encoded:
FOR generations, Fiji football fans have dreamt of seeing the national team compete on football’s biggest stage, the FIFA World Cup, and that ambition could become a reality within the next decade.

Fiji Football Association CEO Mohammed Yusuf says achieving World Cup qualification will require patience, planning and continued investment as the country competes against 211 FIFA member associations fighting for a place at the global tournament.

Yusuf says the Fiji FA has adopted a long-term approach focused on strengthening the sport from the grassroots level through to the elite pathway.

He says the progress made in recent years reflects the foundation being built, with Fiji qualifying for FIFA youth tournaments since 2017, giving young players valuable exposure against international opposition.

According to Yusuf, Fiji’s continued success at the youth level highlights the effectiveness of the development pathway and provides confidence that the country is moving in the right direction.

A major focus has been the expansion of youth competitions through the McDonald’s league, which provides structured tournaments for under-14, U16 and U19 players.

Yusuf says the growth of school’s football, including U18 competitions, along with support from employers, is also playing an important role in identifying and nurturing talented players from an early age.

Beyond player development, Yusuf says infrastructure remains a key priority as Fiji looks to create an environment capable of producing international-level footballers.

Development work at Lomaloma Stadium and plans for a high-performance centre, including a FIFA-supported artificial pitch expected to begin construction in stages between August and October, are part of efforts to provide players with better training facilities.

Yusuf says competing regularly in Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) competitions continues to provide valuable experience for Fiji’s teams as they aim to close the gap with the region’s top football nations.

He believes the combinations of youth development, improved facilities and international exposure can help turn Fiji’s long-standing World Cup dream into reality.

With continued investment and a clear pathway from grassroots football to the national team, Fiji remains hopeful that the senior side can one day earn a place at the FIFA World Cup.

item.title: Boost for Ba golfers
item.description: BA Golf Club will host its third Monthly Medal event this Sunday, with the tournament receiving sponsorship support from Meenoos, Ba. Ba Golf Club has acknowledged Meenoos Company Director Hansraj Parmar for his continued support of the event, which forms part of the club’s build-up towards the prestigious RCM Ba Open.
item.content:encoded:
BA Golf Club will host its third Monthly Medal event this Sunday, with the tournament receiving sponsorship support from Meenoos, Ba.

Ba Golf Club has acknowledged Meenoos Company Director Hansraj Parmar for his continued support of the event, which forms part of the club’s build-up towards the prestigious RCM Ba Open.

Parmar, who plays off a handicap of 13, is a keen golfer and has maintained a strong connection with Ba Golf Club despite frequently travelling between Fiji and Australia.

He regularly represents Ba Golf Club in Theodore events and East versus West tournaments organised by Golf Fiji, where he has also played an important role in leading the club’s B Grade squad.

His support for the club extends beyond this Sunday’s event, with Parmar also pledging further sponsorships before the end of the season.

Ba Golf Club says his continued contribution reflects his passion for golf and commitment to the development of the club.

The Monthly Medal registration will begin at 12.30pm, with tee-off scheduled for 1pm. Entry is $20.

Starters will be Sailesh Kumar, Yash Kumar, Brendan Daniel and Jyoti Lal, while cards will be handled by Damon Chen, Christopher Daniel, Joeli Dakunimata and Pradeep Chandra.

The match committee comprises Rohit Chandra, Rajen Singh, Asish Chand and Manish Patel. Parmar and Ravinesh Chand will conduct the prize presentation.

Meanwhile, attention is already turning to the RCM Ba Open, which will be held on August 15 -16.

Ba Golf Club has confirmed that 65 players have already registered for the tournament, with entries to close once the first 100 players are registered.

Players are being encouraged to secure their places early as the club prepares for another major event on its golfing calendar.

item.title: Breaking barriers through handball
item.description: STEPPING outside their comfort zones and trying new sports is the message from one of Fiji’s young handball representatives as she prepares to take on the world stage in Romania. The Suva Grammar School Form 6 student, Adi Seinimili Logavatu, who hails from Lomanikoro in Rewa with maternal links to Yaroi, Matuku in Lau, is part of the Fiji Under-18 Women’s Handball Team that will create history as
item.content:encoded:
STEPPING outside their comfort zones and trying new sports is the message from one of Fiji’s young handball representatives as she prepares to take on the world stage in Romania.

The Suva Grammar School Form 6 student, Adi Seinimili Logavatu, who hails from Lomanikoro in Rewa with maternal links to Yaroi, Matuku in Lau, is part of the Fiji Under-18 Women’s Handball Team that will create history as the first Pacific Island nation to compete at the International Handball Federation (IHF) Women’s Youth World Championship from July 29 to August 9.

Logavatu hopes the team’s historic campaign will inspire more young athletes to explore new sporting opportunities and not be afraid to try something different.

“Most of the young people are just really scared to try new sports, especially handball,” she said.

Her own journey has taken her from a developing sport in Fiji to the biggest stage of her young career, an experience she describes as both rewarding and memorable.

“I’m really happy and grateful for this opportunity. I’m also proud of the girls and how far we’ve come.

“It was not an easy journey, and with the funding, we also struggled a lot. But I’m really grateful for this opportunity and to represent my country.”

Beyond the court, the journey has also helped Logavatu develop important life skills, with time management becoming one of her biggest strengths as she balances national team commitments with her academic responsibilities.

As a Form 6 student preparing for her Year 12 examinations, she said the experience has strengthened her discipline, organisation and commitment.

“I think time management is one good key takeaway for me. As a student, it’s been really hard to balance sports and my academic work, especially with our Year 12 examination coming up.”

With Fiji drawn alongside Croatia, France and Egypt in Group A, Logavatu is looking forward to gaining experience, building friendships and learning from some of the world’s best young handball players.

“One of my key takeaways that I want to get out of this World Cup is to make friends and just enjoy my time there.”

The historic campaign has also strengthened her ambition to continue representing Fiji in future international competitions.

item.title: Historic start for Lautoka primary schools football
item.description: THE Lautoka Primary Schools’ Football Association Inter-Primary Soccer Competition 2026 kicked off on a strong note, with 40 matches played on the opening day across several grades. The competition featured the Suka, Saqamoli, Drua, Tabua boys, Tabua girls and open under-10 girls categories, with schools from across the Lautoka district taking part.
item.content:encoded:
THE Lautoka Primary Schools’ Football Association Inter-Primary Soccer Competition 2026 kicked off on a strong note, with 40 matches played on the opening day across several grades.

The competition featured the Suka, Saqamoli, Drua, Tabua boys, Tabua girls and open under-10 girls categories, with schools from across the Lautoka district taking part.

A major highlight was the introduction of the first U10 girls tournament in the history of the competition.

Five schools, Tavarau Primary School, Drasa Avenue Primary School, Lautoka Methodist Primary School, Lovu Sangam Primary School and Ahmadiyya Muslim Primary School — took part in the inaugural girls’ competition.

The open U10 girls final will see Lovu Sangam Primary School face Ahmadiyya Muslim Primary School.

Lautoka Primary Schools’ Football Association president Shekar Sharan said the introduction of the girls’ competition was an important milestone for primary school football in the district.

The tournament provides young girls with an opportunity to compete at an early age while developing their football skills, confidence, teamwork and sportsmanship.

The opening day also marked the first appearance of Vitogo District Primary School in the inter-primary soccer competition.

Their participation further highlights the continued growth of primary school football in the Lautoka district.

All categories were played in a round-robin format, giving teams multiple opportunities to compete before the top two sides qualified for the finals.

The finals confirmed are Lautoka Arya Samaj Primary School against Tavarau Primary School in the Drua U10 Boys, Drasa Primary School against Ahmadiyya Muslim Primary School in the Saqamoli U10 Boys, and Lautoka Central Primary School against Lautoka Methodist Primary School in the Suka U10 Boys.

In the Tabua boys final, Teidamu Primary School will meet Shiri Ram Govind Primary School, while Lovu Sangam will face Ahmadiyya Muslim Primary School in the open Under-10 girls final.

The Tabua girls competition was completed on the opening day, with Shiri Ram Govind Primary School crowned champions after finishing ahead of Teidamu Primary School.

With 40 matches completed, the association said the opening day demonstrated the enthusiasm and commitment of players, teachers, coaches, officials and schools towards the development of primary school football in Lautoka.

item.title: EPL race heats up
item.description: THE race for the 2026 Extra Premier League title reaches another crucial stage this weekend as round 16 promises tough competition across the country. League leaders Ba will be looking to maintain their place at the top after another impressive outing last weekend after a 4-1 victory against Lautoka FC. The Men in Black know there is little room for error with Labasa keeping the pressure on.
item.content:encoded:
THE race for the 2026 Extra Premier League title reaches another crucial stage this weekend as round 16 promises tough competition across the country.

League leaders Ba will be looking to maintain their place at the top after another impressive outing last weekend after a 4-1 victory against Lautoka FC. The Men in Black know there is little room for error with Labasa keeping the pressure on.

The Babasiga Lions have shown they are capable of grinding out results after a 1-0 win against Navua FC, and will be eager to capitalise on any slip-up in the title race.

Former champions Rewa also remain firmly in contention and cannot afford to drop points after a draw against Nadi FC last weekend with competition now reaching an important stage.

Round 16 is expected to deliver another weekend of fast-paced football, with title contenders chasing valuable victories and underdogs hoping to upset the competition’s heavyweights.

Fans can expect intense battles as the Extra Premier League edges closer to its conclusion.

The main focus for this week’s round will be the clash between the Men in Black (Ba) and Babasiga Lions (Labasa). The match will determine whether Ba will maintain its first-place position in the league standing or will Labasa finally take lead.

item.content:encoded:
THE McDonald’s Fiji Fijian Drua Women utility back Josivini Naihamu emerged as the biggest winner of the night, claiming both the Encore Players’ Player of the Year and the prestigious McDonald’s Fiji Player of the Year awards during the annual awards at the Sofitel Resort and Spa last night.

Voted by her teammates for the Players’ Player accolade, Naihamu was also selected by head coach Mike Legge as the club’s outstanding performer of the season.

Naihamu enjoyed a superb campaign this season, scoring five tries in six appearances while consistently leading by example through her work ethic, commitment and influence within the squad.

item.title: ‘Lions’on glory hunt | Grammar shifts focus to national knockout
item.description: SUVA Grammar School (SGS) has quickly shifted its attention to the Vodafone Deans Under-18 national elimination rounds after successfully defending its Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Union title. The defending champion edged Nasinu Secondary School 29-22 in Saturday’s final to retain their regional crown, giving the side valuable momentum heading into the next stage of the competition.
item.content:encoded:
SUVA Grammar School (SGS) has quickly shifted its attention to the Vodafone Deans Under-18 national elimination rounds after successfully defending its Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Union title.

The defending champion edged Nasinu Secondary School 29-22 in Saturday’s final to retain their regional crown, giving the side valuable momentum heading into the next stage of the competition.

Team manager Evia Turaganivalu said the players were emotional after the victory and credited their success to faith and the commitment shown throughout the season.

“The team is a bit emotional now and we give back all the glory to God,” she said.

“He has been the main strength that has been pushing this team forward and for today we would like to thank Him and give back the glory and honour to Him for His blessings upon this team.”

Despite the achievement, Turaganivalu said the team would remain focused as they prepare for the national challenge.

“We’ll just take each day as it comes and continue with our preparation.”

SGS will now face Northern Zone fourth-placed side Ratu Luke Secondary School at midday on Saturday at either at Buckhurst Grounds or Suva Grammar grounds in the Vodafone Deans U18 national elimination round. In other U18 national elimination fixtures, Eastern Zone champions Lelean Memorial School will face Marist Brothers High School at midday at Saint Vincent College ground in Natovi, while Ratu Kadavulevu School will take on Ratu Sukuna Memorial School at 1.30pm. The Western Zone eliminations at Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka will see Ba Provincial Freebird Institute face Queen Victoria School at 10am, followed by Cuvu College against St John’s College at 1pm.

In the Southern Zone, Nasinu Secondary School will meet Holy Cross College at midday, while the North Zone eliminations at Ganilau Park in Savusavu will see Shri Guru Nanak Khalsa College face Ratu Navula College before Navatu Secondary School takes on Ra High School.

With the regional stage complete, SGS will now focus on building towards the national quarter-finals as they continue their pursuit of another Vodafone Deans U18 title.

item.title: Rokobuli sets sights on top finish
item.description: THE Nadi Police Rugby Club have achieved its first major target of the season by securing promotion to the Super Premier competition. The side has claimed the DEII Challenge Trophy and intends to defend it for the remainder of the season.
item.content:encoded:
THE Nadi Police Rugby Club have achieved its first major target of the season by securing promotion to the Super Premier competition.

The side has claimed the DEII Challenge Trophy and intends to defend it for the remainder of the season.

Team manager Jason Rokobuli says the side is determined to finish the job by claiming top spot in the TISA Insurance Nadi Rugby Union Competition.

Police sit second on the standings with 63 points after 16 rounds last weekend, trailing leaders Nawaka Rugby on 72 points.

Both teams, along with Korotabu Rugby at 3rd place with 60 points have secured its promotion to the Super Premier grade next season.

Rokobuli said the club entered the season with clear objectives and was pleased to have already achieved one of them.

“Our target at the start of the season was to finish in the top four, and we have managed to do that,” he said.

“We are the owners of the DEII Challenge Trophy now and we are keeping it this year. The next target is to try and top the Premier table so we can challenge for the TISA Insurance Trophy in the Super Premier category, which is currently held by Naduruniu Rugby Club.”

Despite several key players being unavailable due to higher representative duties, Rokobuli remains confident in the squad’s depth.

He said many of the club’s top players are involved with the McDonald’s Nadi Rugby team and the Western Police side, leaving the remaining squad members with an opportunity to step up.

“We are relying on the boys we have now to do the job for us this week and in the next game,” he said.

Rokobuli urged his players to remain committed to the goals established before the season began.

“I just want the boys to stay focused on the targets we set before the season. We know they can do the job for us.”

Rokobuli called on the public to continue supporting the Fiji Police Force in its fight against crime, saying rugby provides young people with opportunities to build better futures.

“Through rugby, youths are getting opportunities to secure jobs overseas, earn a living and create a better future for themselves. That is one positive way we can help steer them away from drugs and crime,” he said.

From the TISA Insurance Nadi Rugby Union Super Premier category, Naduruniu Rugby along with Mosi Rugby, Korobebe Rugby and Nabila Rugby have been demoted to the Premier category next season.
